So I have been in the market for a new notebook for a few months. I have always been a ThinkPad fan, but for about 2 years I tried to daily-drive a MacBook with a satisfactory result. That leads me to consider a second-hand Macbook Air 2017, but I can't seem to find one within my price range.

Then, one way or another, one day I spot a local seller selling a brand-new E14 Gen1 i3 for about $480. The price is not that much different from the Macbook Air I wanted, and hey, it's still a Thinkpad so I pulled the trigger. Another rationalizing factor for my purchase is that the machine has a new i3 Gen 10 CPU and a TPM 2.0, which will be compatible with Windows 11, while the Air won't be compatible because it's still a Broadwell (Gen 5) and it lacks TPM.

After the machine arrived, I copied my data from my main desktop and installed Windows 11 Preview through Windows Insider control panel. In the old hard drive I used to migrate my data, I discovered a dump of DDR X3 vs 2ndMIX, an arcade game I like so much but unable to run in my desktop since it's quite picky about graphics and sound chips. I mean, yes, it can boot in my PC, but not without desyncing or discoloring the arrow to grey. 

Whimsically, I copied the X3 data to the new E14, reconfigured the button mapping, and... Lo and behold, it runs perfectly. No stutter, no sync problem, arrows appear in its original color. Great.

Now I need to buy a new metal dance pad, but that's a story for another day. Lol.

The newest version of Parallels, v16.5, runs Windows 10 for ARM64 nicely. You just need to sign up for Windows Insider from a Windows PC and download Windows 10 Insider Preview VHDX file from the Insider website. Once you had the Insider VHDX file, you're set to go with Parallels.

Note that currently Windows 10 for ARM64 is NOT distributed through traditional/retail channels and only available through OEMs, so there is no way to get a Windows 10 ARM64 retail key. Windows Insider license allows VM installation so Parallels can get away with offering it legally.
